note: Round 1 taxonomy. Every record in this round is a web-search title, so pains are named from thread and question titles on BiggerPockets, Wall Street Oasis and Quora. A pain is a problem the room states, not a topic.

pains.label: CoStar and the other paid data tools cost too much for a small investor
pains.definition: The writer asks whether CoStar, a paid LoopNet membership, Crexi Intelligence or Reonomy is worth the money, what it costs, or wants a cheaper or free alternative.

pains.label: I want to buy my first warehouse or start in commercial and don't know where to start or if it's worth it
pains.definition: A beginner or owner-occupier is deciding whether a warehouse is a good buy, what it would earn, and how to begin; includes 'bought one, now what'.

pains.label: I can't find good industrial deals; how do I find off-market properties
pains.definition: The writer wants deals that are not picked over on LoopNet: off-market sourcing, cold calling owners, finding the first deal.

pains.label: I don't know how to underwrite an industrial or NNN deal
pains.definition: Questions about cap rates, NOI, NNN lease analysis, whether a property's income is real, how long underwriting should take, and whether a modelling course such as the A.CRE Accelerator is worth paying for.

pains.label: What to check before I close: Phase 1 environmental, appraisal, red flags on the building
pains.definition: Diligence on an industrial building or NNN lease before closing, including the Phase I environmental site assessment and the appraisal and what they cost.

pains.label: Getting a commercial loan for a warehouse: down payment, pre-approval hurdles, lenders for NNN, SBA 504, structuring with partners
pains.definition: The writer is trying to finance a warehouse or commercial building and hits a lender, down-payment or structure problem.

pains.label: How do I raise equity for my first syndication or deal
pains.definition: Sponsor-side questions about finding investors and raising money for a deal, including buying with no money down.

pains.label: How to raise (or help raise) money without breaking SEC rules or needing a broker licence
pains.definition: Co-GP and finder's-fee arrangements, JV structures with money partners, Reg D 506(b)/(c), accredited-investor verification, Form D and blue-sky filings.

pains.label: The PPM, operating agreement and syndication attorney cost thousands; what do I need and when
pains.definition: Cost and timing of syndication legal documents and term structuring; wanting a template instead of paying a lawyer.

pains.label: Syndications fail and people lose money; I fear my deal going bad
pains.definition: Stories of failed syndications, doubts whether syndication really pays, distrust of sponsors.

pains.label: Tracking investor commitments, distributions and updates by hand; which syndication software is worth it
pains.definition: The sponsor needs a portal or system to manage investors and asks which software to buy.

pains.label: My warehouse or flex space sits empty and I can't find a tenant or get a good rent
pains.definition: Finding tenants for an empty warehouse or godown, leasing to large companies, covering the mortgage while the building is empty.

pains.label: Should I build or convert to small-bay flex space, and is it still viable
pains.definition: Developing, converting to, or building-to-sell flex or small-bay industrial: viability, sizing, cost.

pains.label: Management fees and CAM on an NNN industrial building: what's fair and what can I pass through
pains.definition: Running an NNN or flex building: property-management fee levels, CAM charges, and whether fees can be passed to tenants.

pains.label: Is a cost segregation study worth its price on a building my size
pains.definition: Whether and when to pay for a cost segregation study to accelerate depreciation.

pains.label: The 1031 exchange 45-day and 180-day clocks and finding a replacement property
pains.definition: Identification and closing deadlines of a 1031 exchange, nominating properties, moving from residential into commercial, failed exchanges.

pains.label: In India, is building or buying a godown or warehouse worth it: what does it cost and what rent will it fetch
pains.definition: Indian owners and would-be owners asking about the cost of building a godown, expected returns, and how to lease it to large companies.
